hero.subtitle: Sofia. Bulgarian and German military surplus, cut into rare civilian pieces.

manifest.body: Bulgarcamo works from Bulgarian and German military surplus, from the Cold War to the years that followed — tarpaulins, canvas bags, sometimes uniforms — sourced in Bulgaria. Each piece is cut from the original textile and sewn in Sofia. When the material runs out, the piece leaves the catalogue.

motifs_section.title: Three camouflages, one raw material
motifs_section.intro: Three prints sourced from Bulgarian and German military textile, reworked into everyday pieces and EDC accessories.

frogskin.name: Frogskin
frogskin.subtitle: Жабешка кожа
frogskin.provenance: Coveralls for airborne and chemical troops.
frogskin.description: Bright green spots and brown rain straits on a grey background. Introduced circa 1968 alongside the splinter pattern, on the same coverall cut, possibly to confuse NATO forces. The coveralls were later reissued to border troops.

splinter_1991.name: Splinter 91
splinter_1991.provenance: Fifth and last version of the Bulgarian splinter, issued across the whole armed forces.
splinter_1991.description: Dark green and dark brown angular shapes on an olive ground, crossed by thin rain stripes. A lineage that began during or just after the Second World War, derived from the German Splittertarnmuster.

dpm.name: Bulgarian DPM
dpm.provenance: Introduced just after Bulgaria joined NATO in 2004.
dpm.description: Black, russet, medium olive and light olive shapes on a pale green or khaki ground, five colours in total. Based on the British DPM, first fielded by units serving in the Balkans, then the standard pattern of the whole armed forces until 2018.

flecktarn.name: German Flecktarn
flecktarn.provenance: Developed in 1976 and tested the same year in the Bundeswehr's Truppenversuch 76 trials, issued across the Bundeswehr from 1990.
flecktarn.description: Five colours in spots: light green, light olive, dark green, brown and black. The European reference for temperate camouflage. In 2018 Bulgaria introduced the M18, a digital hybrid pattern with a palette very close to Flecktarn.

paragraphs: Bulgarcamo works from Bulgarian and German military surplus, from the Cold War to the years that followed — tarpaulins, canvas bags, sometimes uniforms — sourced in Bulgaria. The patterns are not chosen for their aesthetic but for their trace: existing materials, dated, identifiable, irreproducible.
The current release works with three of them — Bulgarian DPM and Splinter, German Flecktarn. Each piece is cut from the original textile and sewn in Sofia, by a neighbourhood seamstress.
Quantity depends on what the surplus allows — a few pieces each season, sometimes a single example. When the material runs out, the piece leaves the catalogue and stays there, marked as withdrawn.

What was an object of war becomes a civilian piece, without making a manifesto of the gesture. There is nothing to imitate, nothing to print, nothing to reproduce. There is a material that already exists, dated and identifiable, and a hand that takes from it to make something else.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: What data this site processes, why, for how long, and how to exercise your rights.

sections.title: Data controller
body: Simon Beltran (Bulgarcamo personal project), Sofia, Bulgaria.
Contact: contact@bulgarcamo.com.

sections.title: Data processed
body: This site offers no accounts, no payments, no forms and no audience measurement, and it keeps no database. The only data involved is:
Technical logs: on each visit, the host Vercel records technical data (IP address, date and time, page requested, browser).
Emails: if you choose to write to contact@bulgarcamo.com, your email address and the content of your message are received in Bulgarcamo’s mailbox.
Instagram messages: if you write to @bulgarcamo on Instagram, your message is received and handled within Instagram.

sections.title: Why, and on what basis
body: Technical logs: running and securing the site. Legal basis: legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Emails: replying to your message. Legal basis: legitimate interest in replying to messages received (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Instagram messages: handling your order request. Legal basis: steps taken at your request (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR).

sections.title: How long data is kept
body: Technical logs: a limited period set by Vercel in its own policy.
Emails: twelve months after the last exchange, then deleted.
Instagram messages: kept within Instagram under Meta’s policy. You can ask at any time for the conversation to be deleted on our side.

sections.title: Host and transfer outside the EU
body: The site is hosted by Vercel Inc., based in the United States, so technical logs may be transferred outside the European Union.
Vercel states that these transfers rely on the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework and on the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses.

sections.title: Orders through Instagram
body: Orders are placed only by Instagram message. Once on Instagram, Meta’s privacy policy applies. Order messages are used only to handle your request.

sections.title: Cookies
body: This site sets no cookies and uses no audience measurement. This is why no consent banner is shown.

sections.title: What your rights are
body: Under the GDPR, you have the following rights:
To exercise them, write to contact@bulgarcamo.com. You will receive a reply within one month.

sections.title: Supervisory authority
body: You can lodge a complaint with the Bulgarian Commission for Personal Data Protection (Комисия за защита на личните данни, КЗЛД), cpdp.bg.
If you live in another EU member state, you can also contact the supervisory authority of your country.
